title: just-deliver environment definition
description: What `jd env up` provisions for an environment: substrate requirements (matched by catalog mappings exactly like workload requirements) and the layout of the environment descriptor written from their outputs. Checked against the catalog, not here: the type is declared, and a type with `approval: true` carries the `approval` block. Rules the schema cannot express: effective requirement ids are unique, and the rules of environment.schema.json hold for the composed descriptor (checked before anything is created).

name.description: Environment name; same pattern as the descriptor's.

type.description: An environment type the catalog declares.

requires.description: Substrate the environment needs, declared by type like a workload's requirements.

id.description: Referenced as ${resource.<id>.<export>}; defaults to the type.

values.description: The descriptor's values layout: nested mappings whose leaves are expressions, normally ${resource.<id>.<export>}. They are merged into the base descriptor's values; a key already there is an error.

approval.description: The gate: an environment with this block accepts deploys only through `jd promote`. A set is promoted when it is qualified on `qualifiedOn` and `required` distinct listed approvers approved it. Literals, not expressions. Rules the schema cannot express: `qualifiedOn` is not this environment and `required` is at most the number of approvers.

qualifiedOn.description: The environment whose records must show the set qualified.

approvers.description: Entra object ids (lower case) that may approve.

separateFromDeployer.description: An approver may not be a principal that deployed the label on `qualifiedOn`. Required: a default would be a silent weakening.

grantable.description: Dot paths under the composed values (base included) that workloads may grant on; added to the base descriptor's.
